# asc metadata sync

Use this skill to keep App Store metadata in sync with App Store Connect. Prefer the canonical `asc metadata` workflow for app-info and version localization fields. Use the lower-level `asc localizations` and `asc migrate` commands only when the user specifically needs `.strings` files or legacy fastlane-format metadata.

## Current canonical workflow

### 1. Pull canonical metadata

```bash
asc metadata pull --app "APP_ID" --version "1.2.3" --platform IOS --dir "./metadata"
```

If the app has multiple app-info records, resolve the app-info ID first and pass it explicitly:

```bash
asc apps info list --app "APP_ID" --output table
asc metadata pull --app "APP_ID" --app-info "APP_INFO_ID" --version "1.2.3" --platform IOS --dir "./metadata"
```

### 2. Edit local files

Canonical files are written under:

- `metadata/app-info/<locale>.json` for app-level fields: `name`, `subtitle`, `privacyPolicyUrl`, `privacyChoicesUrl`, `privacyPolicyText`
- `metadata/version/<version>/<locale>.json` for version fields: `description`, `keywords`, `marketingUrl`, `promotionalText`, `supportUrl`, `whatsNew`

Copyright is not a localization field. Manage it with:

```bash
asc versions update --version-id "VERSION_ID" --copyright "2026 Your Company"
```

### 3. Validate before upload

```bash
asc metadata validate --dir "./metadata" --output table
```

For subscription apps, include the extra Terms of Use / EULA heuristic:

```bash
asc metadata validate --dir "./metadata" --subscription-app --output table
```

### 4. Preview and apply

Run a dry run first:

```bash
asc metadata push --app "APP_ID" --version "1.2.3" --platform IOS --dir "./metadata" --dry-run --output table
```

Apply after the plan looks correct:

```bash
asc metadata push --app "APP_ID" --version "1.2.3" --platform IOS --dir "./metadata"
```

Use `asc metadata apply` when the user wants the apply-named command shape for the same canonical files:

```bash
asc metadata apply --app "APP_ID" --version "1.2.3" --platform IOS --dir "./metadata" --dry-run
asc metadata apply --app "APP_ID" --version "1.2.3" --platform IOS --dir "./metadata"
```

For a review-artifact workflow with explicit approval before mutation, use the metadata review commands introduced in `asc` 2.6.1:

```bash
asc metadata plan --app "APP_ID" --version "1.2.3" --platform IOS --dir "./metadata" --review-dir ".asc/metadata/review"
asc metadata approve --review-dir ".asc/metadata/review" --all
asc metadata status --review-dir ".asc/metadata/review" --output table
asc metadata apply --app "APP_ID" --version "1.2.3" --platform IOS --dir "./metadata" --review-dir ".asc/metadata/review" --confirm
```

Use `asc metadata approve --key "version:en-US:whatsNew"` or `--scope app-info,version` when the user wants selective approval artifacts before the guarded apply.

## Keyword-only workflow

Use this when only the version-localization `keywords` field should change:

```bash
asc metadata keywords diff --app "APP_ID" --version "1.2.3" --platform IOS --dir "./metadata"
asc metadata keywords apply --app "APP_ID" --version "1.2.3" --platform IOS --dir "./metadata" --confirm
```

For importing keyword research:

```bash
asc metadata keywords import --dir "./metadata" --version "1.2.3" --locale "en-US" --input "./keywords.csv"
asc metadata keywords sync --app "APP_ID" --version "1.2.3" --platform IOS --dir "./metadata" --input "./keywords.csv"
```

## Quick field updates

For one-off version-localization edits, pass an explicit version selector. Use `--version-id` for deterministic updates when you already have it, or `--version` plus `--platform` when working from a version string.

```bash
asc apps info edit --app "APP_ID" --version-id "VERSION_ID" --locale "en-US" --whats-new "Bug fixes and improvements"
asc apps info edit --app "APP_ID" --version "1.2.3" --platform IOS --locale "en-US" --description "Your app description here"
asc apps info edit --app "APP_ID" --version "1.2.3" --platform IOS --locale "en-US" --keywords "keyword1,keyword2,keyword3"
asc apps info edit --app "APP_ID" --version "1.2.3" --platform IOS --locale "en-US" --support-url "https://support.example.com"
```

For app-info fields, prefer the post-create setup command:

```bash
asc app-setup info set --app "APP_ID" --primary-locale "en-US" --privacy-policy-url "https://example.com/privacy"
asc app-setup info set --app "APP_ID" --locale "en-US" --name "Your App Name" --subtitle "Your subtitle"
```

## Lower-level localization files

Use `.strings` files when the user specifically wants import/export files instead of canonical JSON:

```bash
asc localizations list --version "VERSION_ID" --output table
asc localizations download --version "VERSION_ID" --path "./localizations"
asc localizations upload --version "VERSION_ID" --path "./localizations" --dry-run
asc localizations upload --version "VERSION_ID" --path "./localizations"
```

For app-info localizations:

```bash
asc apps info list --app "APP_ID" --output table
asc localizations list --app "APP_ID" --type app-info --app-info "APP_INFO_ID" --output table
asc localizations download --app "APP_ID" --type app-info --app-info "APP_INFO_ID" --path "./app-info-localizations"
asc localizations upload --app "APP_ID" --type app-info --app-info "APP_INFO_ID" --path "./app-info-localizations" --dry-run
asc localizations upload --app "APP_ID" --type app-info --app-info "APP_INFO_ID" --path "./app-info-localizations"
```

## Legacy fastlane metadata

Use this only for existing fastlane-format trees:

```bash
asc migrate export --app "APP_ID" --version-id "VERSION_ID" --output-dir "./fastlane"
asc migrate validate --fastlane-dir "./fastlane"
asc migrate import --app "APP_ID" --version-id "VERSION_ID" --fastlane-dir "./fastlane" --dry-run
asc migrate import --app "APP_ID" --version-id "VERSION_ID" --fastlane-dir "./fastlane"
```

## Character limits

| Field | Limit |
|-------|-------|
| Name | 30 |
| Subtitle | 30 |
| Keywords | 100 comma-separated characters |
| Description | 4000 |
| What's New | 4000 |
| Promotional Text | 170 |

## Agent behavior

- Start with `asc metadata pull` unless the user specifically asks for `.strings` or fastlane metadata.
- Always run `asc metadata validate` before remote writes.
- Preview remote changes with `--dry-run` when the command supports it.
- Use `asc metadata plan` plus `approve`/`status` when the user wants a durable review artifact before apply.
- For quick edits, always pass `--version-id` or `--version` plus `--platform`; do not rely on ambiguous latest-version behavior.
- Keep app-info fields and version fields separate.
- Use `--output table` for human verification and JSON for automation.

#!/bin/bash
# Run the App Store Connect CLI against the release credentials.
#
#   mise run asc -- apps list
#   mise run asc -- builds list --app 6799644194
#
# The three values asc wants are the three release.env already carries, under
# other names — so nothing is stored twice and no keychain profile is created.
# asc resolves a stored profile first and falls back to the environment, which
# means a hand-made `asc auth login` keeps winning over this wrapper.
set -euo pipefail

# shellcheck source=Scripts/release-env.sh
. "$(dirname "$0")/release-env.sh"
require_asc_key

export ASC_KEY_ID="$REACHY_ASC_KEY_ID"
export ASC_ISSUER_ID="$REACHY_ASC_ISSUER_ID"
export ASC_PRIVATE_KEY_PATH="$REACHY_ASC_KEY_PATH"
# Piped output is JSON either way; this only decides what a terminal shows.
export ASC_DEFAULT_OUTPUT="${ASC_DEFAULT_OUTPUT:-table}"

exec asc "$@"

Готово. Все три URL-а обновлены на сервере, локальные `metadata/` уже были правильными — расхождение было именно между репозиторием и App Store Connect.

**Что изменено в App Store Connect:**

| Место | Поле | Было → Стало |
|---|---|---|
| App Information (общее) | Privacy Policy URL | `github.com/.../blob/main/docs/privacy.md` → `…github.io/reachy-mini-swift/privacy.html` |
| Версия 0.2.1 **iOS** | Marketing / Support URL | `github.com/...` / `.../issues` → сайт `/` и `/support.html` |
| Версия 0.2.1 **macOS** | Marketing / Support URL | то же самое, отдельным пушем |
| TestFlight (`betaAppLocalizations`) | Marketing / Privacy URL | `github.com/...` → сайт `/` и `/privacy.html` |

Проверено: повторный `--dry-run` по обеим платформам показывает пустой diff, все три страницы сайта и публичная TestFlight-ссылка отдают 200.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
Две вещи, на которых легко потерять изменения:
1. `metadata push` **не трогает TestFlight** — `betaAppLocalizations` хранит собственную копию marketing/privacy, вне `metadata/` и вне любой версии. Формально это отдельный ресурс API, поэтому «обновил витрину» ≠ «обновил бету», и тестировщики продолжали бы видеть старые ссылки.
2. Локализация версии живёт **на платформу**, а не на приложение: у iOS и macOS 0.2.1 разные `localizationId` (`18b91dcc…` и `ae7ac5bd…`). Пуш только с `--platform IOS` молча оставил бы macOS на github.com — состояние, которое `--dry-run` для iOS показывает как «чисто».
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

Два наблюдения, которые стоит знать, но которые я не трогал:
- **macOS 0.2.1 в состоянии `REJECTED`**, iOS 0.2.1 — `WAITING_FOR_REVIEW`. Правку URL-ов Apple приняла в обоих состояниях, вытаскивать версию из ревью не понадобилось.
- В ASC ещё нет версии 0.2.2, хотя релиз в репозитории уже зашит (`866d9b0`), и каталог `metadata/version/` содержит только `0.2.1`.

`docs/release.md` поправлен (не закоммичен): текст утверждал, что `metadata/` теперь указывает на сайт «для обоих», что читается как «TestFlight обновится сам» — заменил на явное «`metadata push` туда не доходит» с командой. Сказать — закоммичу.
Хватит умничать с циклом — два прямых вызова.

`./bin/mise run asc -- … --output json | python3 …` never parses: mise prints its own
`[asc] $ …` echo line truncated to terminal width and without a trailing newline, so the
JSON is glued onto it and neither `grep '^{'` nor `json.load` sees a document. Piping

For anything machine-readable, drop the task wrapper:

```bash
eval "$(./bin/mise env -s bash)"
./Scripts/asc.sh localizations list --version "$ID" --output json | python3 -c '…'
```

`./bin/mise x -- ./Scripts/asc.sh … --version <id>` is not the workaround — `mise x`
swallows `--version` itself and asc then reports it as missing.

Related: [[asc-cli-wiring]].

# App Store submission health

Use this skill to explain why a release cannot proceed and to manage an existing review submission. Hand healthy release execution back to `asc-release-flow`.

## Ownership boundary

This skill owns:

- readiness validation and blocker diagnosis;
- public-API, web-session, and manual repair routing;
- review status and history;
- cancellation and retry decisions.

Do not stage, upload, publish, or submit a healthy release from this skill.

## Answer order

1. State whether the version is ready, blocked, or already under review.
2. Name each blocker and the evidence that proves it.
3. Separate public-API repairs from web-session and manual work.
4. Give one next command. Do not dump the entire repair catalog.

## Establish the target

- Resolve `APP_ID`, the version string or `VERSION_ID`, `BUILD_ID`, platform, and any known `SUBMISSION_ID`.
- Configure auth with `asc auth login` or `ASC_*` environment variables.
- Use `ASC_BYPASS_KEYCHAIN=1` only for repository tests and isolated verification, not normal user sessions.
- Prefer IDs once the target is resolved; stop when app, version, or product resolution is ambiguous.

## Diagnose readiness

Run the canonical readiness report first:

```bash
asc validate --app "APP_ID" --version "1.2.3" --platform IOS --output table
```

Use `--version-id "VERSION_ID"` when known. Add `--strict` when warnings must fail automation.

Ask the review-specific doctor for an ordered explanation:

```bash
asc review doctor --app "APP_ID" --version "1.2.3" --platform IOS --output table
```

Collect direct evidence when the report points at the build or version:

```bash
asc builds info --build-id "BUILD_ID" --output table
asc versions view --version-id "VERSION_ID" --include-build --include-submission --output table
```

For digital goods, run only the relevant product validator:

```bash
asc validate iap --app "APP_ID" --output table
asc validate subscriptions --app "APP_ID" --output table
```

Treat the ordered remediation plan from `asc validate` as the repair queue. Fix and verify one class of blocker before moving to the next.

## Route repairs

Use public API commands when the blocker is build processing, metadata, screenshots, review details, encryption, content rights, age rating, availability, or version-scoped product metadata.

Read [references/readiness-repairs.md](references/readiness-repairs.md) when diagnostics identify one of those common blockers or a first-release availability gap.

Read [references/digital-goods.md](references/digital-goods.md) only when IAP or subscription validation fails, Apple requires first-review attachment, or a versioned product must join an existing review submission.

Read [references/app-privacy.md](references/app-privacy.md) only when validation reports an App Privacy advisory or the publish state cannot be confirmed through the public API.

When validation reports a Game Center component or version blocker, hand it to `asc-release-flow` and request the multi-item reference's **Prepare every item** section. Do not route Game Center through general readiness or digital-goods repairs.

Use the web-session commands only for a gap the public API cannot cover, and say that an authenticated Apple web session is required. Keep a manual App Store Connect fallback when the user declines web-session automation.

## Decide whether the version is healthy

A version is ready to return to `asc-release-flow` when:

- `asc validate` has no blocking issues;
- the attached build is `VALID`;
- metadata, screenshots, app info, review details, content rights, encryption, age rating, pricing, and availability are resolved;
- the relevant `asc validate iap` and/or `asc validate subscriptions` checks have no blocking issues, and the required digital-goods versions are prepared;
- any Game Center version items have been checked through `asc-release-flow`'s multi-item submission reference;
- App Privacy is confirmed or published.

Do not call a version ready merely because one validator exits successfully. Report any warning that still needs a web-session or manual check.

## Monitor review

Use app-scoped status when the submission ID is unknown:

```bash
asc review status --app "APP_ID" --version "1.2.3" --platform IOS --output table
```

Use exact submission or version IDs when available:

```bash
asc submit status --id "SUBMISSION_ID" --output table
asc submit status --version-id "VERSION_ID" --output table
```

Use the release dashboard for surrounding build and review signals:

```bash
asc status --app "APP_ID" --include builds,appstore,submission,review --output table
```

Use history to distinguish a current stall from earlier rejected or completed submissions:

```bash
asc review history --app "APP_ID" --version "1.2.3" --paginate --output table
```

## Cancel an unhealthy submission

Resolve the exact active submission before cancelling. Preview status first, then require confirmation:

```bash
asc submit status --id "SUBMISSION_ID" --output table
asc submit cancel --id "SUBMISSION_ID" --confirm
```

When resolving by version, include the app for the modern review-submission lookup:

```bash
asc submit status --version-id "VERSION_ID" --output table
asc submit cancel --version-id "VERSION_ID" --app "APP_ID" --confirm
```

The lower-level equivalent is valid when the exact review submission is already known:

```bash
asc review submissions-cancel --id "SUBMISSION_ID" --confirm
```

Do not cancel a submission solely because review is taking longer than expected. Confirm the state and the user's intent first.

## Decide when to retry

There is no dedicated retry command. Use this sequence:

1. Cancel only if the active submission must be withdrawn.
2. Repair the proven blockers.
3. Re-run `asc validate` and the relevant product validators.
4. Confirm no active submission already owns the version or review items.
5. Hand the healthy version and any preserved `SUBMISSION_ID` to `asc-release-flow` for submission execution. Reuse an inspected `READY_FOR_REVIEW` draft; create a submission only when no matching draft or active submission exists.

## Common failure routing

| Symptom | First evidence | Repair route |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Version is not in a valid state | `asc validate`, `asc review doctor` | ordered readiness repairs |
| Export compliance must be approved | build info and encryption declaration | readiness repairs |
| Multiple app infos found | `asc apps info list --app "APP_ID"` | resolve exact app-info ID |
| IAP or subscription is not ready | product validator | digital-goods reference |
| Game Center component or version is not ready | `asc validate` diagnostic | `asc-release-flow` multi-item preparation section |
| App Privacy publish state is unclear | validation advisory | App Privacy reference |
| Review appears stuck | review status plus history | monitor; cancel only with evidence and approval |

## Guardrails

- Do not use removed `submit-preflight` or `submit-create` shortcuts.
- Do not submit from this skill; return healthy execution to `asc-release-flow`.
- Do not treat web-session automation as public App Store Connect API coverage.
- Do not retry until the earlier submission state and blocker repairs are verified.
- Use `--output table` for human diagnosis and JSON for automation.
- For macOS, use `--platform MAC_OS` while keeping the same health lifecycle.

fix(macos): sign-in crash, camera stream, and the geometry of the viewport controls (#90)

* fix(camera): drop ICE's end-of-candidates marker before RTCIceCandidate

The robot's gstreamer webrtcsink sends an empty candidate to mark the end of
gathering, and `RTCIceCandidate.init` answers that with
`NSParameterAssert(sdp.length)` — an `NSException`, which `try?` does not
catch, thrown by an argument that is evaluated before `peerConnection?.add`
is ever reached. So the app was killed on the ordinary path, the moment the
robot *finished* gathering: `Invalid parameter not satisfying: sdp.length`,
`RTCIceCandidate.mm:28`.

Both signalling paths funnel into that one construction site, so one guard
covers the LAN and the relay alike. `iceCandidate` is its own function
because `handle(_:)` cannot be tested for this: `peerConnection?.add` is an
optional chain, so with no peer the argument is never evaluated and the
broken version survives the very call that killed it in production.

Adds `com.apple.security.network.server`: ICE binds UDP sockets and receives
datagrams from a peer it never connected() to, which App Sandbox counts as
inbound. Without it the bind is refused before the firewall is consulted, the
stream never leaves `.connecting`, and the 10 s watchdog renegotiates for
ever.

* fix(hf): stop assuming the main actor in the web auth callbacks

Signing in killed the app on macOS with no exception, no `Fatal error`,
nothing on stderr and no crash report — `dispatch_assert_queue` aborts
through `abort_with_payload`, which is none of those. The only trace is
`BUG IN CLIENT OF LIBDISPATCH: Assertion failed: Block was expected to
execute on queue [com.apple.main-thread]`, and it is in the log for the
*shipping* 0.2.1 build as well as for a local one.

Two places assumed an actor they were not on, and only one of them is
visible in the source:

- `presentationAnchor(for:)` is `nonisolated` and answered with
  `MainActor.assumeIsolated`, which is an assertion rather than a hop.
  AuthenticationServices calls it from a queue of its own. The anchor is now
  chosen on the main actor before `start()` and simply handed back.
- The completion handler is written inside a `@MainActor` method and the
  ObjC block parameter is not `@Sendable`, so Swift 6 infers the enclosing
  isolation and wraps it in the same assertion — with nothing in the body to
  point at. `@Sendable` makes it nonisolated, which is what it always was.

Hopping instead is not available: the protocol requirement is synchronous,
and a `@preconcurrency` conformance only spells the same trap differently.

Also brings the app back to the front once the browser closes. Safari holds
the front slot and macOS hands it to whatever is behind rather than back to
us; under Stage Manager that is another stage entirely, so the window did not
merely lose focus, it left the screen. `activate()` alone does nothing there —
it takes the front only when nobody else holds it.

* fix(ui): state the size and shape of the viewport and account controls

Every one of these derived its geometry from whatever glyph happened to be

--- notes:
Hey Reachy is a network client for the Reachy Mini Wireless, a physical desktop robot made by Pollen Robotics. It is an unofficial, independent client, not affiliated with or endorsed by Pollen Robotics, and it talks only to the robot's own HTTP/WebSocket daemon over the local network.

HARDWARE REQUIRED

Most of the app sits behind a live connection to a robot, and we have no way to hand you one. With no Reachy Mini on the same Wi-Fi network the app stays on its Connect screen: the five main tabs (Robot, Live, Moves, Apps, Settings) are not instantiated until a handshake with a robot's daemon succeeds. There is no demo mode, no mock data and no test account, because the app has no backend of its own and no accounts of its own. The App Store description states this requirement in its second paragraph.

FIRST LAUNCH, PLEASE READ

A Bluetooth setup sheet opens automatically over the Connect screen on the very first launch. Dismiss it with Cancel: the iOS Local Network permission alert is waiting underneath it. Please allow that one. The app uses Bonjour to find robots on the local network and does nothing else with it.

WHAT YOU CAN EVALUATE WITHOUT THE ROBOT

1. Connect screen. Three segments: "This network" (Bonjour discovery, which will stay on "Searching..."), "Hugging Face", and "Manual". Under Manual, type any host and tap Connect to exercise the real failure path ("Couldn't connect to ...", Try again, Cancel).
2. Privacy permissions, from the button at the bottom of the Connect screen. Grant or refuse Bluetooth, Local network and Microphone; each carries an explanation and a link to Settings.
3. "Set up a new robot over Bluetooth". The first two steps work without hardware: a prerequisites screen, then a scan that finds nothing.
4. Hugging Face sign-in, from the account button in the top left. This is the one feature that works end to end without a robot. It signs in to the reviewer's own huggingface.co account through OAuth in a web sheet, stores the token in the Keychain, and uses it to list robots the account has linked for remote access and to install robot apps from Hugging Face Spaces. Any huggingface.co account works. Nothing is collected: there is no server on our side.

PERMISSIONS

Local Network: to find the robot over Bonjour and reach its daemon. Required for the app's purpose.
Bluetooth: only to put a brand-new robot onto Wi-Fi, requested when the user taps Start in that flow.
Microphone: only to talk through the robot's speaker during a live session, requested on demand.
Camera: the app never records with the device's camera. The usage string is declared because the WebRTC stack that receives the robot's video references the API.

NAME AND TRADEMARK

"Reachy Mini" is a product name of Pollen Robotics, used here solely to describe what this app is compatible with. Both the App Store description and the project's public README state that the app is unofficial and unaffiliated.

Contact: Aleksei Kakoulin, akakoulin.dev@gmail.com, +7 778 909 8053. Happy to answer anything, including on a video call showing the app driving a real robot.

## Что удалось установить

| Факт | Значение | Откуда |
|---|---|---|
| Submission | `be50e844…`, отправлена **2026-08-13 18:41:43Z** | `review submissions-list` |
| Состояние | `UNRESOLVED_ISSUES`, элементов — 1, он `REJECTED` | `review items-list` |
| Отклонённый элемент | сама версия macOS 0.2.1, не IAP и не Game Center | `--include appStoreVersion` |
| Состояние версии | **`REJECTED`**, не `METADATA_REJECTED` | `versions view` |
| Сборка на ревью | 138, залита 18:07:33Z | `builds info` |
| Валидатор сейчас | **0 блокирующих ошибок**; только пустой `whatsNew` (warning) и «App Privacy не проверяем публичным API» (info) | `asc validate`, `review doctor` |

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
`REJECTED` и `METADATA_REJECTED` — два разных состояния в машине состояний App Store Connect, и разница здесь диагностическая. `METADATA_REJECTED` означает претензию к листингу: правится текст, новый бинарник не нужен. Простой `REJECTED` означает, что претензия к самому приложению — краш, недоступная функциональность, невозможность провести ревью.

То есть **дело не в описании, не в скриншотах и не в URL-ах**, которые я только что менял. Ревьюер запускал приложение.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

## Одну версию удалось снять — краш при входе

`Scripts/release-macos.sh:68` задаёт `BUILD_NUMBER="$(git rev-list --count HEAD)"`, то есть номер сборки — это счётчик коммитов, и сборка однозначно отображается в коммит:

```
build 134   93b31a6  chore(release): ship 0.2.1
build 138   acaf765  fix(macos): sign-in crash, camera stream, ...  ← ушло на ревью
build 139   866d9b0  chore(release): ship 0.2.2
```

Сборка 138 — это ровно `acaf765`, коммит, который чинит падение при входе через Hugging Face (`BUG IN CLIENT OF LIBDISPATCH`) и краш камеры на ICE. Подозрение было сильным, потому что заметки для ревью прямо направляют ревьюера в этот сценарий: «Hugging Face sign-in… **this is the one feature that works end to end without a robot**». Но на ревью ушёл уже починенный бинарник — **эта версия отпадает**.

Побочный факт, который стоит знать: под маркетинговой версией 0.2.1 уехал код, которого в теге `0.2.1` нет (`acaf765` содержится только в `0.2.2`). Сборка 134 — это тег, сборка 138 — main спустя 6,5 часов.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
iOS несёт **ту же самую сборку 138** и до сих пор `WAITING_FOR_REVIEW` — её просто ещё не смотрели. Так что «macOS отклонили, а iOS нет» пока не означает, что проблема macOS-специфична: это означает только, что macOS попала в очередь первой. Ожидать того же вердикта по iOS — разумно.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

## Чего у меня нет

Текста отклонения в публичном API нет вообще: переписка живёт в Resolution Center, а туда есть только web-сессионный доступ. `asc web auth status` отвечает `{"authenticated":false}`, а вход требует Apple ID с 2FA — в неинтерактивной сессии это невыполнимо. Почту тоже проверил: подключён `alexey1312ru@gmail.com`, а уведомления ASC уходят на `akakoulin.dev@gmail.com` — писем от Apple здесь нет.

Два способа получить причину дословно:

```bash
mise run asc -- web auth login --apple-id akakoulin.dev@gmail.com
mise run asc -- web review show --app 6799644194 --apple-id akakoulin.dev@gmail.com
```

или просто письмо «App Review — Rejected» в ящике `akakoulin.dev@gmail.com` за 13–14 августа.

## Что я ставлю первым кандидатом

**Guideline 2.1, App Completeness — ревьюер не смог провести ревью без робота.** Это гипотеза, а не факт, но она единственная согласуется со всеми уликами: бинарное отклонение, чистый валидатор, и наши собственные заметки для ревью, где написано буквально «Most of the app sits behind a live connection to a robot, and we have no way to hand you one. There is no demo mode, no mock data and no test account». Обычный ответ Apple на это — требование демонстрационного видео работы с железом.

И отдельно, независимо от причины: **заметки для ревью написаны под iOS**, а прочитал их macOS-ревьюер. Там про «Bluetooth setup sheet opens automatically over the Connect screen», про «the **iOS** Local Network permission alert is waiting underneath it» и про тап по сегментам. Человек на Маке этого не увидит и решит, что инструкция не про то приложение, которое он запустил. Перед повторной отправкой стоит развести notes по платформам и приложить видео с реальным роботом — оно закрывает и 2.1, и вопрос «как это вообще выглядит».

    fix(macos): sign-in crash, camera stream, and the geometry of the viewport controls (#90)
    
    * fix(camera): drop ICE's end-of-candidates marker before RTCIceCandidate
    
    The robot's gstreamer webrtcsink sends an empty candidate to mark the end of
    gathering, and `RTCIceCandidate.init` answers that with
    `NSParameterAssert(sdp.length)` — an `NSException`, which `try?` does not
    catch, thrown by an argument that is evaluated before `peerConnection?.add`
    is ever reached. So the app was killed on the ordinary path, the moment the
    robot *finished* gathering: `Invalid parameter not satisfying: sdp.length`,
    `RTCIceCandidate.mm:28`.
    
    Both signalling paths funnel into that one construction site, so one guard
    covers the LAN and the relay alike. `iceCandidate` is its own function
    because `handle(_:)` cannot be tested for this: `peerConnection?.add` is an
    optional chain, so with no peer the argument is never evaluated and the
    broken version survives the very call that killed it in production.
    
    Adds `com.apple.security.network.server`: ICE binds UDP sockets and receives
    datagrams from a peer it never connected() to, which App Sandbox counts as
    inbound. Without it the bind is refused before the firewall is consulted, the
    stream never leaves `.connecting`, and the 10 s watchdog renegotiates for
    ever.
    
    * fix(hf): stop assuming the main actor in the web auth callbacks
    
    Signing in killed the app on macOS with no exception, no `Fatal error`,
    nothing on stderr and no crash report — `dispatch_assert_queue` aborts
    through `abort_with_payload`, which is none of those. The only trace is
    `BUG IN CLIENT OF LIBDISPATCH: Assertion failed: Block was expected to
    execute on queue [com.apple.main-thread]`, and it is in the log for the
    *shipping* 0.2.1 build as well as for a local one.
    
    Two places assumed an actor they were not on, and only one of them is
    visible in the source:
    
    - `presentationAnchor(for:)` is `nonisolated` and answered with
      `MainActor.assumeIsolated`, which is an assertion rather than a hop.
      AuthenticationServices calls it from a queue of its own. The anchor is now
      chosen on the main actor before `start()` and simply handed back.
    - The completion handler is written inside a `@MainActor` method and the
      ObjC block parameter is not `@Sendable`, so Swift 6 infers the enclosing
      isolation and wraps it in the same assertion — with nothing in the body to
      point at. `@Sendable` makes it nonisolated, which is what it always was.
    
    Hopping instead is not available: the protocol requirement is synchronous,
    and a `@preconcurrency` conformance only spells the same trap differently.
    
    Also brings the app back to the front once the browser closes. Safari holds
    the front slot and macOS hands it to whatever is behind rather than back to
    us; under Stage Manager that is another stage entirely, so the window did not
    merely lose focus, it left the screen. `activate()` alone does nothing there —
    it takes the front only when nobody else holds it.
    
    * fix(ui): state the size and shape of the viewport and account controls
    
    Every one of these derived its geometry from whatever glyph happened to be
    inside it, so each control came out a different size and none of the drawn
    shapes matched the areas that answered a click. Measured at `.title3`:
    `ellipsis.circle` is 33 x 33, `mic.slash` 31 x 34 and `slider.horizontal.3`
    35 x 31 — and `Circle` insets to the *shorter* side, so the discs had three
    diameters and the two oblong glyphs overhung the circle they sat in, which is
    what the stray line across the settings button was.
    
    - `Metrics.viewportControl` states the square: the widest glyph plus
      `Space.sm` on each side, through `@ScaledMetric` so a larger text size does
      not clip it.
    - A `Button` takes `ViewportControlButtonStyle`. A style's body *is* the
      button, so the disc it draws is also what answers a click; the modifier this
      replaces sat outside the button and could set neither — macOS drew the
      button's own rectangle around the glyph and only that rectangle was live.
    - A `Menu` keeps the default style with `.buttonStyle(.plain)` and puts the
      disc on its label. Painting a background straight onto each menu in a real
      window measured the control itself: `.borderlessButton` discards the label's
      layout, `.menuStyle(.button)` imposes 39 x 17 of its own, and only the
      default plus `.plain` honours the label's 36 x 36.
    - The switcher's backing is concentric on macOS rather than a capsule. An
      AppKit segmented control measures 157 x 24 with a ~4 pt corner where a
      capsule would be 12, so the capsule curved away from it and left both a
      crescent and a live corner outside the drawn shape. iOS keeps the capsule
      and the 240 pt cap: only iOS stretches the segments.
    - The toolbar avatar matches what a toolbar symbol measures — 15 x 15, against
      the 26 it was. A toolbar sizes its chrome around a symbol, so signing in
      grew the item's glass into a shape neither round nor a capsule. Two attempts
      at the *shape* moved it and neither settled it, because what disagreed was
      the size.

## Причина

Автоматическая проверка, не живой ревьюер: в macOS-бинарнике есть `com.apple.security.network.server`, а статический анализ не нашёл кода, который слушает входящие соединения.

Мои две гипотезы были мимо — и промах поучительный. Я правильно установил, что это **бинарное** отклонение (`REJECTED`, а не `METADATA_REJECTED`) и что на ревью ушёл именно `acaf765`. Но из этого я сделал вывод «краш починен, значит дело в железе», тогда как верный вывод был противоположным: тот же самый коммит, который чинил краши, **добавил спорное право**.

```
build 138 = acaf765  →  + com.apple.security.network.server
```

Сборка 134 (тег 0.2.1) этого права не несла и до автопроверки бы не дошла. То есть отклонение вызвано ровно тем изменением, которое я разбирал, — я просто читал его diff как «набор фиксов», а не как «изменение поверхности прав».

## Право нужно, убирать нельзя

Обоснование измерено и записано в двух местах — `.claude/rules/networking.md` и комментарий в самом `ReachyMini-macOS.entitlements`: ICE биндит UDP-сокеты и принимает датаграммы от пира, которому не делал `connect()`, а App Sandbox считает это прослушиванием. Без ключа bind отклоняется **до** обращения к файрволу — ни запроса, ни записи в лог, поток навсегда остаётся в `.connecting`, а десятисекундный watchdog `CameraSession` бесконечно перепереговаривается. Убрать право — сломать камеру.

Значит вариант Apple №2, а не №1.

## Что сделано

Добавил раздел в App Review Information macOS-версии (detail `02866a9c…`), 3990 символов из 4000:

> **APP SANDBOX: com.apple.security.network.server** — The app runs no server. This entitlement is required by WebRTC's ICE… ICE binds local UDP sockets and receives datagrams from a peer it never called `connect()` on, which App Sandbox counts as listening. With `network.client` alone the bind is refused before the firewall is ever consulted… Nothing else listens. There is no HTTP or FTP server, no port is published or advertised, and no connection is accepted from any host other than the robot the user has already connected to.

Существующий текст сохранён целиком, раздел вставлен перед `NAME AND TRADEMARK`.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
Заметки для App Review не лежат в `metadata/` — у канонического воркфлоу `asc metadata` их просто нет в схеме. Они существуют только на сервере и привязаны к записи версии. Из этого следует, что при заведении 0.2.2 их придётся написать заново, а проверка автоматическая и сработает снова: сборка 139 несёт то же право.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

## Что остаётся за вами

Ответ в Resolution Center — туда нужен web-сессионный вход с 2FA, из этой сессии недоступен. Текст можно взять тот же:

```
The app runs no server. com.apple.security.network.server is required by WebRTC's
ICE, which carries the robot's camera and two-way audio. The robot runs a gstreamer
webrtcsink and the app is the receiving peer: ICE binds local UDP sockets and
receives datagrams from a peer it never called connect() on, which App Sandbox
counts as listening. With com.apple.security.network.client alone the bind is
refused before the firewall is consulted — no prompt, nothing logged — and the video
stream never leaves its connecting state. Nothing else in the app listens: no HTTP
or FTP server, no published or advertised port, and no connection accepted from any
host other than the robot the user has already connected to. This explanation is now
also in the App Review Information section.
```

Дальше — повторная отправка. iOS-заявку это не касается: `com.apple.security.*` — права App Sandbox, только macOS; сборка 138 на iOS ждёт ревью и к ней претензий нет.

from pathlib import Path

SRC = Path("/Users/aleksei/Downloads/Screenshots/Mac")
OUT = Path("/tmp/mac-shots")

NAMES = {
    "CleanShot 2026-08-13 at 23.13 Background Removed.52@2x.png": "01-live-3d.png",

    "CleanShot 2026-08-13 at 17.09 Background Removed.04@2x.png": "06-connect.png",
}


def gradient(size):
    w, h = size
    img = Image.new("RGB", size)
    px = img.load()
    span = w + h - 2
    for y in range(h):
        for x in range(w):
            t = (x + y) / span
            px[x, y] = tuple(
                round(a + (b - a) * t) for a, b in zip(TOP_LEFT, BOTTOM_RIGHT)
            )
    return img


base = gradient(CANVAS)
OUT.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

for src, name in NAMES.items():
    shot = Image.open(SRC / src).convert("RGBA")
    shot = shot.crop(shot.getchannel("A").getbbox())
    w, h = shot.size
    scale = min(0.88 * CANVAS[1] / h, 0.70 * CANVAS[0] / w)
    shot = shot.resize((round(w * scale), round(h * scale)), Image.LANCZOS)
    canvas = base.copy()
    canvas.paste(
        shot,
        ((CANVAS[0] - shot.width) // 2, (CANVAS[1] - shot.height) // 2),
        shot,
    )
    canvas.save(OUT / name)
    print(f"{name:<16} window {shot.width}x{shot.height} on {CANVAS[0]}x{CANVAS[1]}")

Ваши файлы нельзя было залить как есть — по двум причинам:

**Альфа-канал.** Все шесть пришли `hasAlpha=yes`: CleanShot вырезал обои и оставил прозрачность вокруг скруглённых углов и тени. App Store скриншоты с альфа-каналом не принимает — это отказ на самой загрузке.

**Размер.** `1828×1748` — почти квадрат, а macOS принимает только 16:10: `1280×800`, `1440×900`, `2560×1600`, `2880×1800`. Растягивать нельзя, значит окно нужно класть на холст.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
Обрезка по alpha-bbox здесь не косметика, а то, что определяет геометрию. Исходный кадр нёс разную по величине прозрачную рамку, и центрирование по краям файла посадило бы окно на холсте вразнобой от кадра к кадру. Тень при этом сохраняется: она не прозрачная, а полупрозрачная, и в bbox входит.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

**Фон** взял графитовый градиент приложения — `#9AA6B8 → #3E4757`, те же стопы, что у иконки и у сайта, на который теперь ведут все URL-ы. Signed artifacts are produced locally; CI only publishes the GitHub release with
generated notes. Credentials never enter the repository or CI.

## One-time setup

1. **App Store Connect API key** — App Store Connect → Users and Access →
   Integrations → App Store Connect API → Team Keys, role **App Manager**.
   Download the `.p8` once and write the credentials file:

   ```bash
   mkdir -p ~/.config/reachy-mini
   cat > ~/.config/reachy-mini/release.env <<'CONF'
   REACHY_DEVELOPMENT_TEAM=XXXXXXXXXX
   REACHY_ASC_KEY_ID=XXXXXXXXXX
   REACHY_ASC_ISSUER_ID=xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx
   REACHY_ASC_KEY_PATH=/Users/you/.config/reachy-mini/AuthKey_XXXXXXXXXX.p8
   CONF
   ```

2. **App IDs and the App Group** — the first signed build with
   `-allowProvisioningUpdates` registers the bundle ids
   (`com.alexey1312.ReachyMini`, `.Widget`), but the
   `group.com.alexey1312.ReachyMini` capability must be added by hand in
   Xcode's Signing & Capabilities, once per App ID (app and widget separately,
   iOS and macOS separately). `xcodebuild` cannot create it.

3. **App Store Connect app record** — My Apps → New App:
   - Name: **Hey Reachy**; if taken, fall back to “Hey Reachy — robot remote”.
   - Subtitle: **Control your Reachy Mini**.
   - Bundle id `com.alexey1312.ReachyMini`.
   - The description must state it is an unofficial client for Reachy Mini by
     Pollen Robotics. A public TestFlight link goes through Beta App Review, so
     the name is checked before any App Store submission.
   - App Privacy: no data collected. The app talks to the robot on the local
     network and to Hugging Face with the user's own OAuth session; nothing is
     sent to the developer.
   - Encryption: answered in the Info.plist (`ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption`),
     ASC asks nothing per build.

4. **Developer ID Application certificate** (macOS) — Xcode → Settings →
   Accounts → Manage Certificates → “+” → Developer ID Application.

   signing assets besides the Developer ID certificate: Apple Distribution and
   Mac Installer Distribution. `-allowProvisioningUpdates` creates them through
   the Xcode account the same way it does for iOS. The app record already

`release:macos` archives once and exports that archive twice, because
`-exportArchive` re-signs per method — the two artifacts are the same build:

| Channel        | Method            | Artifact                           | Ends up in              |
| -------------- | ----------------- | ---------------------------------- | ----------------------- |
| `developer-id` | notarize → staple | `Export/macOS/HeyReachy-<ver>.zip` | GitHub release, by hand |
| `appstore`     | upload            | `.pkg` (not kept)                  | TestFlight for macOS    |

Developer ID runs first on purpose: it is the artifact that always ships, and a
failed App Store upload should not also cost you the zip. Pick one channel with
`--channel appstore` or `--channel developer-id`.

Both archive commands compile with the Xcode compilation cache off
(`COMPILATION_CACHE_ENABLE_CACHING=NO`) and then run
`Scripts/check-appintents-metadata.sh` against the archive before anything is

Shortcuts app only ever sees what `appintentsmetadataprocessor` extracted into

error. TestFlight 0.1.1 shipped exactly that way: green archive, no actions in
the Shortcuts app. The check names every missing action instead; if it fails,
the fix is in the build, not in App Store Connect.

Dry runs: `mise run release:ios -- --no-upload` exports an `.ipa` without
uploading; `mise run release:macos -- --no-notarize` stops the Developer ID

leave a `.pkg` in `Export/macOS/AppStore` instead of uploading it. Each flag
belongs to one channel and is ignored by the other.

Что пришлось решить по дороге:

**Версию поднял до 0.2.3.** `MARKETING_VERSION` оставался `0.2.2`, а 0.2.2 уже лежит в TestFlight сборкой 139. Второй бинарник под той же строкой дал бы две разные 0.2.2 в одном списке.

**Загрузка iOS пошла в обход Xcode.** `release-ios.sh` грузит через аккаунт Xcode, который здесь разлогинен, поэтому `--no-upload` плюс `asc publish testflight` — тот самый documented fallback. Он одним вызовом залил, привязал публичную группу и отправил Beta App Review.

**Кейчейн был заперт** — `security show-keychain-info` отвечал `User canceled the operation`. Отпер до сборки, иначе macOS-экспорт умер бы через три минуты в `productbuild` с невнятной ошибкой.
